subject: Estimating personal ability scores in multilevel settings

messages.author: 924bfcf78d0dfcc2
messages.subject: Estimating personal ability scores in multilevel settings
parts:
Dear everyone,

I am trying to estimate personal ability scores of the respondents to a cross-national survey. By using mirt, and particularly its mixedmirt() function, I would like to account for the multilevel nature of the data.


I would really appreciate any help with writing the code for this. Having read the manual and example several times, I am completely stuck.


I have created an example dataset below:

set.seed(125)
df <- data.frame(student = sample(1:1000, 1000, replace = FALSE),
                        school = sample(1:10, 10, replace = FALSE),
                        q1 = sample(0:1, 100, replace=TRUE),
                        q2 = sample(0:1, 100, replace=TRUE),
                        q3 = sample(0:1, 100, replace=TRUE))

where student refers to each respondent, school refers to the grouping variable, and the following three variables (q1, q2, q3) are students' answers to three hypothetical questions. These three variables are binary, coded as 0 for wrong answers and as 1 for right answers.


How would the code look like if I were to estimate the scores for each student, given that they are in different schools?


Many thanks and all the best,


Resul

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Estimating personal ability scores in multilevel settings
parts:
It sounds like you want to use the lr.random input to mixedmirt to create this random effects hierarchy for the ability terms. lr.random accepts formulas, so that's how you would specify each random cluster's structure. 

lr.random = ~1|school

where the student information random effect is automatically included in the structure (IRT models always include these, because that's the point of a measurement model). See the last example in help(mixedmirt) demonstrating this type of two-level structure, as well as the associated paper in JEM. HTH.

Phil
